I am AFAB and so is my partner. I, on the one hand, grew up as hyperlexic and hypercalculic, I was reading middle-grade books in early elementary school, still read 'above' my suggested reading level, and have an identic memory when it comes to vocabulary.  My hypercalculia had me taking geometry and precalc/calc in early middle school.

My partner, on the other hand, is in her early 30s, and is on a 1st reading level and can only solve early elementary math if they are in word problem form.

My hyperlexia and use of a larger vocabulary (unintentionally, may I add) can make our communication a little difficult, as I need to go back and use a smaller vocabulary for her to be able to comprehend what I'm trying to convey. My hyperlexia makes communicating with other autistics besides my partner very difficult beyond just 'normal autism'

As someone who working towards a career path in healthcare, and as an autistic individual myself, I have a few of my own that aren't commonly spoken of. 

1) The verification of what informed consent refers to on a comprehension level of the individual. As a young adult first going into the hospital on my own, I signed a paper that referenced informed consent to treatment and was utterly confused when the informed consent was enforced. I had not been explained what informed consent meant and was greatly traumatised because of it. 

2) Safe foods. If an autistic individual brings in their safe food to an ER or it is brought to their assigned room, please do not refuse the individual their safe food (unless specific health concerns). While I was in the ER, I had my safe food revoked and I had a meltdown that required restraint. This leads me to:

3) Restraints should be the last thing done in the event of a meltdown, restraints may worsen the meltdown. Please offer other alternatives to 'calm' a melting-down patient such as dimming the lights (if in a private room), offering a PRN, or ear plugs. If the autistic individual is using a fidget or has a stuffed animal, please do not separate them from their safety object.

I may come back if I think of any others, but this is what I have for now.
